title: Embedded annotation prefixes break streaming parser in Private VPC flows
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary: Several customers using Private/VPC deployments observe structured tool-call outputs with reordered or misattributed JSON fields when responses are streamed. Root cause appears to be proxy-side annotation prefixes (small ASCII markers injected into the stream for telemetry/correlation) that land in the middle of a streamed token/chunk boundary. Our streaming parser currently treats these annotation bytes as payload and, under certain chunk alignments, shifts field boundaries when reconstructing structured outputs for tool/function calls. This manifests as valid JSON with fields in the wrong object, duplicated keys, or parser failures that fall back to plaintext responses.

Why this matters: customers rely on deterministic structured outputs for tool-calling and downstream routing. Field reordering leads to mis-invocations, data leakage between calls, and production errors in customer services. This has already caused two escalations and one P1 outage for a Private deployment customer using our dedicated proxy stack.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy Private inference with the dedicated proxy that injects per-request annotation markers (marker pattern used by the proxy team: '<<@ann:ID:1234>>').
2) Use a multi-part streaming generator configured for function/tool calling that emits a JSON object via streaming chunks (model with long outputs / intermediate tool streaming is easiest).
3) Configure the proxy to inject the annotation prefix approximately every 1-2KB (simulated production telemetry).
4) Observe the client-side streaming parser reassembling chunks into structured JSON and compare field ordering / attribution against the original non-proxied stream.
5) Trigger with a few different boundary offsets (offsets that split inside nested JSON strings) to reproduce field reordering consistently.
logs: 2026-03-02T09:17:23Z PROXY INFO tenant-acme inject_marker <<@ann:ID:4821>> to stream chunk#42
2026-03-02T09:17:23Z RUNTIME WARN stream-parser chunk-reassembly: boundary-split inside 'tool.payload' at byte 8191 -> created field-shift
2026-03-02T09:17:23Z APPLICATION ERROR tool-invoke tenant-acme 'metadata' attributed to previous tool call id=0x7f1b

After reassembly we saw: '{"tool":{"name":"search","args":{"q":"latest release notes<<@ann:ID:4821>>","filters":{"prod":true}}}}' which shifts the annotation into the args string and breaks downstream JSON-based routing.
impact_summary: High impact for Private and Dedicated customers using proxy telemetry injection. Two active customer escalations (tenant-acme, tenant-zenhealth). Results include misrouted tool calls, duplicated invocations, and at least one customer rollback to hosted mode. Estimated affected surface: ~0.8% of streaming requests in setups that use annotation injection; higher for long-output workloads.
customer_reports: tenant-acme: production errors 2026-03-02 09:15-09:30 UTC, multiple misrouted tool invocations, severity P1
tenant-zenhealth: intermittent structured-output field duplication, degraded user-facing feature (clinical summary generation)
workaround: Temporarily disable proxy annotation injection for tactical mitigation; set proxy telemetry mode to 'post-commit' where markers are emitted as separate control frames (if proxy supports) or route streaming traffic through a non-injecting gateway. Advise customers to pin to non-streaming responses until fix is rolled out.
proposed_fix: 1) Update streaming parser to recognize and strip our canonical annotation pattern when it appears between chunk boundaries without treating it as payload. 2) Make parser chunk-reassembly resilient to ASCII prefix insertions by verifying JSON token continuity across artificial markers. 3) Add end-to-end tests that simulate proxy injection at various offsets. 4) Longer term: collaborate with proxy team to support out-of-band control frames instead of inline prefix injection.
